messages:
kevin (cust): Hey team, ran into a weird one after switching embedding models. Rerank responses are returning near-zero / flat scores for all candidates even though the embeddings look okay on our side. No 4xx/5xx from the API. Anyone seen silent failures like this when you supply embeddings to the rerank endpoint?

maria (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl or python) and the X-Request-ID from the rerank call? Also which embed model + rerank model names you used?

kevin (cust): repro below, pasted sensitive bits replaced. request id: req_0a1b2c3d

```python
# get embedding
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={
  'model': 'embed-xlarge-v2',
  'input': 'The quick brown fox'
}, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'})
emb = resp.json()['data'][0]['embedding']  # len = 1536

# call rerank with precomputed embeddings
rr = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank', json={
  'model': 'rerank-large',
  'query': 'fox',
  'candidates': ['doc a','doc b','doc c'],
  'candidate_embeddings': [emb, emb, emb],
  'embedding_model': 'embed-xlarge-v2'
}, headers={'X-Request-ID': 'req_0a1b2c3d','Authorization': 'Bearer ...'})
print(rr.status_code)
print(rr.json())
```

Result: status 200, body: {"scores": [0.0002, 0.0001, 0.0003]} (values ~1e-4, not meaningful; before switch we saw varied scores like 0.8/0.3/0.1).

maria (support): Thanks — that helps. Two quick checks: 1) confirm len(emb) on your side (you said 1536). 2) what's rerank-large's expected embedding dim in our model catalog? If those don't match, that could explain near-zero dot products. Do you mind sharing the exact model strings you used for both steps?

kevin (cust): Confirmed: len=1536. embed model name: embed-xlarge-v2. rerank model: rerank-large (I picked from the console dropdown). I didn't get any "dimension mismatch" error though — thought we'd get 4xx. Logs from our side show the API accepted the payload and returned scores.

dan (ml-eng): fwiw, rerank models internally use a fixed embedding space (e.g., rerank-large expects 1024-d vectors). Historically we accepted external embeddings without strict runtime checks because we also accept raw text and embed internally. If you pass mismatched-length vectors some internal code path will either truncate/pad or compute dot on mismatched buffers which can lead to near-zero outputs. We should've surfaced an explicit error.

kevin (cust): Ah that would explain it. Is the behavior documented? I didn't see a validation step. We assumed supplying any embedding that came from our embedding API would be compatible.

zoe (eng-runtime): Not currently enforced for all models — we rely on clients to pass embeddings produced by compatible models. That said, this silent failure is bad. Quick triage: can you (kevin) do a quick check and return me the model catalog entry for rerank-large? You can call /v1/models or I can fetch it. Expected dim for rerank-large should be 1024.

kevin (cust): Ran /v1/models/rerank-large -> metadata shows "expected_embedding_dim": 1024. Yep mismatch.

maria (support): Okay two immediate routes: A) short-term: regen embeddings with a 1024-d embed model (e.g., embed-standard-1024) or call rerank with text (let the service embed). B) we escalate to engineering to add server-side validation so the API returns 400 with a clear error like "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536". Which do you prefer?

kevin (cust): I'll regen for now (we have to ship). But we need the validation — this burned us cycles and cost. You can share the repro with eng.

zoe (eng-runtime): Thanks — please cc me. Short-term SDK improvement: we can add client-side validation that queries model metadata and asserts len(embedding) == expected_embedding_dim before sending. I'll open a small PR to add Embedding.validate_dimensions() and a warning in the docs.

dan (ml-eng): For server-side: propose a two-step rollout to avoid breaking customers: 1) telemetry + soft-warning header/warning field returned when dims mismatch, and emit a user-visible warning in the response. 2) after 2 weeks and outreach, switch to hard 400 error. I'll file ENG-487 to track the work (validate + improved error code + documentation).

maria (support): Escalating now. Created ticket SUP-2291 and linked ENG-487. Would you like us to process a usage review / partial credit for the calls that returned bad scores? We can look into billing adjustments once engineering confirms scope.

incidents-bot: New support ticket SUP-2291 created by maria (support). Priority: P2. Linked issues: ENG-487.

kevin (cust): Thanks. Please share ETA. I'll proceed to regen with embed-standard-1024 and report back.

maria (support): ETA: SDK client-side patch in 48–72h, server-side soft-warning rollout within 3 days, hard 400 enforcement planned in ~2 weeks after outreach. We'll follow up in this thread and update SUP-2291.

kevin (cust): Appreciate it — will try the regen and post results.

zoe (eng-runtime): One more repro tip for the team: add a cheap local assert in examples: `assert len(embedding) == model_catalog['expected_embedding_dim'], 'embedding dim mismatch'`. Saves a lot of smoky debugging.

maria (support): Marking this thread resolved for now; will reopen if you still see issues after regen. Thanks everyone!
